articles.titleTr: Borsada şirketlerden peş peşe hamleler! Milyonluk anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar gündemde
articles.summaryTr: Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören 8 şirket, yayımladıkları KAP açıklamalarıyla yeni iş ilişkileri, stratejik anlaşmalar ve yatırımlara imza attıklarını duyurdu.
articles.articleText: Borsada şirketlerden peş peşe hamleler! Milyonluk anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar gündemde Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören 8 şirket, yayımladıkları KAP açıklamalarıyla yeni iş ilişkileri, stratejik anlaşmalar ve yatırımlara imza attıklarını duyurdu. LINK, 11,5 milyon TL'lik yüz tanıma kamerası projesini tamamladı Link Bilgisayar, Emniyet Genel Müdürlüğü ile imzaladığı 11 milyon 554 bin TL bedelli KGYS yüz tanıma kamerası projesini tamamladı. Şirket, teslimat ve faturalandırma işlemlerinin gerçekleştirildiğini KAP'a bildirdi. EUPWR, TEİAŞ ihalesinde 205,9 milyon TL'lik teklifle birinci oldu Europower Enerji, TEİAŞ'ın 152 adet metal clad hücre ve yedek malzeme alımı ihalesinde en avantajlı teklifi vererek ilk sırada yer aldı. İhalenin baz bedeli 205 milyon 917 bin TL olarak açıklandı. QNBFK'den 75 milyon euroluk kredi anlaşması QNB Finansal Kiralama, uluslararası kalkınma finansmanı kuruluşu Proparco ile 75 milyon euro tutarında kredi anlaşması imzaladı. İş Leasing'den 100 milyon euro ve 30 milyon dolarlık kredi anlaşması İş Finansal Kiralama, Hollanda Kalkınma Bankası FMO liderliğindeki sendikasyon kapsamında 100 milyon euro ve 30 milyon dolar tutarında kredi sözleşmesi imzaladı. Kaynağın yeni katılımcıyla 50 milyon dolara kadar artırılması mümkün olacak. SAYAS'tan Endonezya'ya 1,3 milyon euroluk sipariş Say Yenilenebilir Enerji'nin Endonezya merkezli müşterisi PT. Kenertec Power System'e verdiği teklifler onaylandı. Toplam 1 milyon 315 bin 914 euro tutarındaki siparişin teslimatlarının 2027'nin ilk çeyreğinde tamamlanması bekleniyor. FONET, Hatay'da 216,7 milyon TL'lik ihaleyi kazandı Fonet Bilgi Teknolojileri, Hatay İl Sağlık Müdürlüğü tarafından düzenlenen 36 aylık sağlık bilgi yönetim sistemi hizmet alımı ihalesinin kazananı oldu. İhalenin bedeli 216 milyon 681 bin 840 TL olarak açıklandı. TAV Havalimanları, TAV Batum'un tamamını 3 milyon dolara satın aldı TAV Havalimanları, TAV Batum'daki yüzde 24'lük payı 3 milyon dolara devraldı. Satın alma sonrası şirketin TAV Batum'daki ortaklık oranı yüzde 76'dan yüzde 100'e yükseldi. GEN İlaç'tan 5 milyar TL'lik enerji yatırımı! Seleda'nın yüzde 81,4'ünü aldı Gen İlaç, biyogaz ve güneş enerjisi alanında faaliyet gösteren Seleda Biyogaz'ın yüzde 81,4'lük payını 5 milyar 27 milyon TL bedelle devraldı. Pay devir işlemleri 13 Kasım'da tamamlandı.

articles.title: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
articles.summary: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
articles.summaryTr: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.
articles.articleText: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge - Published Senator Chuck Schumer is facing a challenge to his position as US Senate majority leader from his fellow Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen, as the party prepares to take control of Congress after sweeping the midterm elections. Van Hollen, 67, said in a post on X on Thursday that Americans voted for change earlier this month and "to deliver, we need new leadership". Schumer, 75, has led Democrats in the chamber since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader. He was first elected to the Senate in 1999. Following the midterms earlier this month, his position has come under pressure by some left-wing Democrats who see him as too moderate and part of the party establishment. Responding to the challenge, Schumer, who represents New York, said he welcomed "any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead". He added that he was "proud of what we've accomplished together" in the midterms, and he had "the votes to continue as Democratic leader". The vote on Senate leader will be held behind closed doors in early December and the winner will assume the role on 4 January, when Democrats take control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives after their midterms successes. The move by Van Hollen, who represents Maryland, marks the most significant step by a high-profile Democrat to challenge the party's existing leadership following last week's midterms victory. Announcing his plans to run in a post on X, he wrote that Americans had called on the party to "unrig an economy rigged against working people". "We should not be preserving our institutions if they are not delivering for the American people," he said at a summit in Colorado hosted by majority Democrats. "And we should be making delivering for the American people the single mission of our government, even when that means shaking things up." He added: "This country does not belong to the people who can afford to buy influence. It belongs to all of us. And it's time we govern like that." In recent years, Van Hollen has taken positions popular with those on the left of his party. In 2024, he supported restricting weapons shipments to Israel and criticised the Biden administration over its role in the war in Gaza. In an interview with MS NOW, Van Hollen - who has served in the Senate for nearly a decade - acknowledged that he was an "underdog" but added that he believed the race was "very much in flux". Independent Senator Bernie Sanders and Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed have both publicly come out in support of Van Hollen - while others have also called for new leadership. In a post on X, Sanders said he believed Van Hollen "will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families". El-Sayed said the challenger would bring "bold leadership" and lead with both "courage and experience". Others Democrats have publicly backed Schumer. Senator Jacky Rosen of Nevada said: "He has the experience and the fight to continue leading our diverse caucus at this crucial moment". Senator Kirsten Gillibrand said: "You will see, despite all the grumblings, enormous gratitude for the hard work he has done to get us to this position." - Published18 hours ago - Published1 day ago - Published2 days ago

articles.articleText: COP31’de sanat ve iklim krizi buluştu: Altı sanatçıdan ortak çağrı - Antalya’da düzenlenen COP31 kapsamında sanat ve iklim krizi COPArt’ta buluştu. Altı sanatçının eserlerinden oluşan seçki, geri dönüştürülmüş metallerden doğanın kırılganlığına uzanan çalışmalarla insanın çevreyle ilişkisini ve gezegenin geleceğini sorguluyor. RS Sanat Alanı, Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği 31. Taraflar Konferansı (COP31) kapsamında Antalya’da düzenlenen COPArt’ta sanatseverlerle buluşuyor. 20 Kasım’a kadar konferansın Green Zone ve Blue Zone alanlarında ziyaret edilebilen seçki; iklim acil durumunu, doğanın kırılganlığını ve insanın çevresi üzerindeki etkisini sanatın düşündüren, sorgulatan ve harekete geçiren diliyle gündeme taşıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle RS Sanat Alanı, COPArt’taki seçkisiyle iklim acil durumuna ilişkin tartışmalara sanatın özgün bakışını da katıyor. Sanatçılara verdiği destekle farklı ifade biçimlerine alan açarken ziyaretçileri ortak bir soru etrafında buluşturuyor: Doğayla kurduğumuz ilişkiyi değiştirmek için neyi görmemiz, neyi hatırlamamız ve neyi dönüştürmemiz gerekiyor? Asaf Erdemli, Berkan Baycan, Ceylan Sakin Dökmen, Gönül Nuhoğlu, İsmet Doğan ve Murat Uçar’ın eserlerini, COP31 katılımcılarıyla buluşturan RS Sanat Alanı, farklı sanat pratiklerinin çevresel ve toplumsal meseleler etrafında diyalog kurmasına destek veriyor. Doğa, hafıza, dönüşüm ve aidiyet kavramları etrafında şekillenen çalışmalar, ziyaretçilerin insanın dünyadaki yerine ve diğer canlılarla ilişkisine yeniden bakmasını sağlıyor. Asaf Erdemli, “Bu İşte Bir Terslik Var” adlı enstalasyonunda Türkiye’nin doğal ve kültürel mirasının simgelerinden ters laleyi, geri dönüştürülmüş metaller aracılığıyla yeniden yorumluyor. COP31 kapsamında özel olarak üretilen 31 adet ters lale heykelinden oluşan enstalasyon, üretim ve tüketim alışkanlıklarımızı sorgularken, atıl malzemelerin yeniden değer kazanmasına dikkat çekiyor. Sanatçı, geri dönüşümü yalnızca bir üretim yöntemi olarak değil, doğaya ve geleceğe karşı kolektif bir sorumluluk olarak ele alıyor. Berkan Baycan’ın “Observer” adlı video çalışmasında bakışın yönü değişiyor: İnsan doğayı izlerken doğa da insanın yaptıklarına tanıklık ediyor. İnsan merkezli düşünceyi sorgulayan eser, ziyaretçiyi doğadaki dönüşümün sorumluluğunu paylaşan bir aktör olarak kendi konumunu değerlendirmeye çağırıyor. Ceylan Sakin Dökmen’in “Güneş Ağacı”, “Rüzgara Kapıldım” ve “Ağıt Ağaç” adlı metal heykelleri, doğanın kırılganlığı ile yenilenme gücünü aynı yüzeyde buluşturuyor. Eserlerdeki çatlaklar ve boşluklar, kırılmanın izlerini taşırken yeniden oluşun ihtimalini de barındırıyor. Sanatçı, metalin sertliği üzerinden doğanın hassas dengelerine dikkat çekiyor. Gönül Nuhoğlu’nun “Dreaming Rhino” adlı çalışmasındaki uyuyan gergedan, iklim krizi karşısındaki kolektif kayıtsızlığın simgesine dönüşüyor. Eser, büyüyen tehditlerin gündelik yaşam içinde nasıl sıradanlaştığını sorgularken izleyiciyi kendi duyarsızlıklarıyla yüzleşmeye davet ediyor. İnsan doğaya baktığında yalnızca çevresini değil, kendi kökenlerini de görüyor. İsmet Doğan, “Kök-en” ve “Autos” serisinde insanın doğayla, geçmişiyle ve kendi varoluşuyla kurduğu bağı sorguluyor. Kökler, doğaya ait bir yaşam kaynağı olmanın yanı sıra hafızanın, kimliğin ve aidiyetin simgesi olarak beliriyor. İzleyiciyi kendi yansımasıyla eserin bir parçasına dönüştüren sanatçı, insanın doğayla bir bütün olduğunu hatırlatıyor. İklim krizinin doğayla kurduğumuz ilişkiyi yeniden düşünmeye zorladığı günümüzde, “Kök-en” temel bir soruyu gündeme getiriyor: İnsan, kendi köklerinden ne kadar uzaklaşabilir? Murat Uçar’ın eserleri, Türkiye tarihinde ilklere imza atmış 36 ismin yaşamına büyüteç aracılığıyla yakından bakmaya davet ediyor. Kolektif hafızayı şekillendiren öncü figürleri yeniden görünür kılan eserler, değişimin ardındaki insan hikâyelerini seçkinin odağına taşıyor.

articles.titleTr: BMW'den 721 bin araç için yangın alarmı! Park uyarısı geldi
articles.summaryTr: ABD Ulusal Kara Yolu Trafik Güvenliği İdaresi (NHTSA), yangın riski nedeniyle BMW'nin yaklaşık 721 bin aracını geri çağırdığını duyurdu. Araç sahiplerine, onarım işlemi tamamlanana kadar otomobillerini açık alana park etmeleri uyarısı yapıldı.
articles.articleText: BMW'den 721 bin araç için yangın alarmı! Park uyarısı geldi - ABD Ulusal Kara Yolu Trafik Güvenliği İdaresi (NHTSA), yangın riski nedeniyle BMW'nin yaklaşık 721 bin aracını geri çağırdığını duyurdu. - Araç sahiplerine, onarım işlemi tamamlanana kadar otomobillerini açık alana park etmeleri uyarısı yapıldı. ABD Ulusal Kara Yolu Trafik Güvenliği İdaresi (NHTSA), Alman otomobil üreticisi BMW'nin 720 bin 796 aracını yangın riski nedeniyle geri çağırdığını açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle NHTSA tarafından yapılan açıklamada, söz konusu araçların park halindeyken ve motoru kapalıyken de yangın riski taşıdığı belirtildi. Araç sahiplerine, gerekli onarım tamamlanana kadar otomobillerini binalardan ve diğer araçlardan uzakta, açık alanlara park etmeleri tavsiye edildi. 2024'te de geri çağrılmışlardı Açıklamada, geri çağırma kapsamındaki araçların 2024 yılında su pompası kaynaklı bir sorun nedeniyle de servise çağrıldığı hatırlatıldı. Mevcut sorunun giderilmesi için araçların yeniden onarılması gerektiği bildirildi. Soruna yönelik çözümün henüz geliştirme aşamasında olduğu belirtilirken, onarım hizmetinin hazır olduğunda BMW yetkili servislerinde ücretsiz olarak sunulacağı kaydedildi. Geri çağırma hangi BMW modellerini kapsıyor? Geri çağırma kararı, 2012-2016 model yılları arasındaki bazı BMW 3 Series ve 5 Series araçlarının yanı sıra X1, X3, X4 ve X5 modellerini de kapsıyor. NHTSA'nın açıkladığı listede ayrıca Z4, 2 Series ve 4 Series modellerinin belirli üretim yıllarındaki coupe, convertible, Gran Coupe ve Sportswagon versiyonları da yer alıyor. Geri çağırma kapsamındaki araç sahiplerinin, araçlarının bu listede bulunup bulunmadığını şasi numarası (VIN) üzerinden kontrol etmesi ve onarım süreciyle ilgili BMW'den gelecek bilgilendirmeleri takip etmesi gerekiyor.

articles.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
articles.summary: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
articles.summaryTr: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.
articles.articleText: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost? - Published A major Microsoft outage has impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world. Services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot, are being restored almost 24 hours since issues first surfaced. Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue. It has apologised for the disruption. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. What happened? Some Microsoft 365 services have been affected by "connectivity problems" with problems reported in at least 74 countries. From late on Thursday, customers reported varying levels of access - many were unable to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. But some users were able to use Teams, messaging and online meeting functions without issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added that it was focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" but warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues". In a later statement, the company said it was continuing to see improvements "with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels". The company attributed the ongoing outage to an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions," it said on Friday. Will emails affected by the outage ever arrive? Although services are beginning to resume, Microsoft has warned of continued "intermittent access issues", meaning some users will still struggle to load their inboxes and could experience "delayed email delivery". In other words, it is not quite safe to assume every email you send is going to arrive in its intended recipient's inbox right away. Earlier, Microsoft said it would be extending the "timeout window" to 48 hours "to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up". The email timeout window refers to the amount of time Outlook will wait to receive an email. When they do show up, the timestamp will be when they were delivered rather than when they were sent. Why has it taken so long to fix? Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time. Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues. "What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said. "The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs. "One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in. "You can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit." The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online. Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time". He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal. Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. "Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. "Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said. In a statement, Microsoft said it was "deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. "We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services." How many people have been affected? More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website. The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed. Microsoft 365 is used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services. Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic both earlier reported problems as a result of the outage. articles.articleTextTr: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost? - Published A major Microsoft outage has impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world. Services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot, are being restored almost 24 hours since issues first surfaced. Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue. It has apologised for the disruption. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. What happened? Some Microsoft 365 services have been affected by "connectivity problems" with problems reported in at least 74 countries. From late on Thursday, customers reported varying levels of access - many were unable to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. But some users were able to use Teams, messaging and online meeting functions without issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added that it was focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" but warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues". In a later statement, the company said it was continuing to see improvements "with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels". The company attributed the ongoing outage to an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions," it said on Friday. Will emails affected by the outage ever arrive? Although services are beginning to resume, Microsoft has warned of continued "intermittent access issues", meaning some users will still struggle to load their inboxes and could experience "delayed email delivery". In other words, it is not quite safe to assume every email you send is going to arrive in its intended recipient's inbox right away. Earlier, Microsoft said it would be extending the "timeout window" to 48 hours "to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up". The email timeout window refers to the amount of time Outlook will wait to receive an email. When they do show up, the timestamp will be when they were delivered rather than when they were sent. Why has it taken so long to fix? Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time. Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues. "What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said. "The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs. "One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in. "You can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit." The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online. Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time". He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal. Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. "Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. "Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said. In a statement, Microsoft said it was "deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. "We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services." How many people have been affected? articles.title: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
articles.summaryTr: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
articles.articleText: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own - Published Pope Leo XIV has celebrated mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities. The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff. "Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers. "Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago. Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the mass began. "We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique. Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend. Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting. Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional. The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached. They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C. For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight. "The Pope has come home and Chiclayo is celebrating," said Lisbeth Díaz, a teacher who worked with Pope Leo when he served as the city's bishop between 2015 and 2023. Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the pontiff, who was elected in May 2025. The trip has also taken in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in this country carries particular significance. The Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities. Around Chiclayo, it is hard to meet anyone who doesn't claim to be a friend of the Pope or have a special anecdote about him. Some recall how he would enjoy sampling Peruvian delicacies at El Trébol, a restaurant next to the city's cathedral. Others remember his love of tennis. But for many it's the more serious moments of his time here, such as helping launch soup kitchens during the Covid-19 pandemic, or wading through deep waters on horseback when floods hit the area. Several of these images are on display in a small museum dedicated to him at the entrance to the bishop's residence. But for the city, and for a country that calls him the "Peruvian Pope", his return home means much more than a collection of photographs and anecdotes. "It is the return of the man who brought Peruvians closer to the Church," said Samuel David Miranda Atoche, a local parish priest from Chiclayo who was ordained by the Pope back when he was still the bishop and known under his birth name of Robert Prevost. And it is not just local people he connected with, according to Díaz, who came to Chiclayo from Venezuela. "It was difficult for him to see so many migrants living on the streets," she added, recalling the time when large numbers of Venezuelans came through Chiclayo escaping the political and economic crisis in their home country. "So, he got in touch with the migration authorities and coordinated with other organisations to speed up the paperwork needed for many of us to obtain legal residency and work permits." - Who is Robert Prevost, the new Pope Leo XIV? - Published9 May 2025 Robert Prevost's time here as bishop also involved difficult decisions, such as having to deal with the controversy and scandal surrounding the dissolution of Sodalitium of Christian Life, a Peruvian Catholic organisation that had faced decades of sexual abuse allegations. Santiago Roncagliolo, a Peruvian writer and journalist who has studied the Pope's life, believes his handling of that crisis earned him the favour of his predecessor, Pope Francis, and helped set him on the path to the papacy. Father David also stressed the role the now-pontiff played in bringing people together. "If there is one thing Bishop Prevost worked for here," he added, referring to the Pope by his previous title, "it was unity". That unity has been on display in the run up to the mass, with the square in front of Chiclayo Cathedral filled with joyous celebrations for days. Normally, 800,000 people live in the city and its surrounding area, but estimates say the Pope's visit has caused that to double. Local businesses have been capitalising on the Pope's popularity to boost sales and hotels have sharply increased their nightly room rates. But that didn't seem to put off the faithful who gathered for the mass. Shouts of: "The Pope is from Chiclayo!" echoed across the field during the event. Their affection was clearly reflected by the pontiff. "As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart," he said from the stage, "for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life." articles.titleTr: 3 şirketten SPK'ya başvuru! Halka arz, birleşme ve sermaye tavanı hamleleri
articles.summaryTr: 12-13 Kasım tarihlerinde 3 şirket, farklı kurumsal işlemler kapsamında Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'na (SPK) başvurduğunu KAP üzerinden duyurdu. Başvurular arasında halka arz, kolaylaştırılmış birleşme ve kayıtlı sermaye tavanı artırımı öne çıktı.
articles.articleText: 3 şirketten SPK'ya başvuru! Halka arz, birleşme ve sermaye tavanı hamleleri - 12-13 Kasım tarihlerinde 3 şirket, farklı kurumsal işlemler kapsamında Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'na (SPK) başvurduğunu KAP üzerinden duyurdu. - Başvurular arasında halka arz, kolaylaştırılmış birleşme ve kayıtlı sermaye tavanı artırımı öne çıktı. SPK'ya üç şirketten halka arz, birleşme ve sermaye tavanı başvurusu geldi. Başvurular arasında yeni bir halka arz hazırlığı da yer aldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 12-13 Kasım 2026 tarihlerinde SPK'ya başvuru yapan şirketler ve başvuru konuları şöyle: Investco Holding (INVES) Investco Holding'in yüzde 100 bağlı ortaklığı REM Girişim Sermayesi Yatırım Ortaklığı'nın halka arz başvurusu, 12 Kasım 2026 tarihinde SPK'ya yapıldı. Ata Turizm (ATATR) Ata Turizm, yüzde 100 bağlı ortaklıkları Gökyüzü Balonculuk Taşımacılık Hizmetleri ve Kapadokya Balonculuk Ticaret Turizm şirketlerini devralmak üzere SPK'ya başvurdu. Başvuru, iki şirketin tüm aktif ve pasifleriyle birlikte tasfiyesiz şekilde Ata Turizm bünyesinde birleştirilmesini kapsıyor. Birleşmenin kolaylaştırılmış usulde gerçekleştirilmesi planlanıyor. Loras Holding (LRSHO) Loras Holding, kayıtlı sermaye tavanını 1,2 milyar TL'den 15 milyar TL'ye yükseltmek için SPK ve Ticaret Bakanlığına başvurma kararı aldı. Yeni kayıtlı sermaye tavanının 2027-2031 yılları arasında 5 yıl süreyle geçerli olması planlanıyor. Bu kapsamda şirket esas sözleşmesinin sermayeye ilişkin 7. maddesinin değiştirilmesi de kararlaştırıldı. Kayıtlı sermaye tavanı, şirketlerin esas sözleşmelerinde belirlenen ve yönetim kurulu kararıyla çıkarılmış sermayenin artırılabileceği üst sınırı ifade ediyor. Tavanın yükseltilmesi doğrudan sermaye artırımı yapıldığı anlamına gelmiyor.

articles.titleTr: Türkiye Sigorta'dan fon soruşturması kapsamında 1,6 milyar TL'lik ödeme
articles.summaryTr: Türkiye Sigorta (TURSG), tasfiyeye konu bazı yatırım fonlarından elde ettiği kazancın 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin 908 TL'lik bölümünü TMSF'ye iade etti.
articles.articleText: Türkiye Sigorta'dan fon soruşturması kapsamında 1,6 milyar TL'lik ödeme - Türkiye Sigorta (TURSG), tasfiyeye konu bazı yatırım fonlarından elde ettiği kazancın 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin 908 TL'lik bölümünü TMSF'ye iade etti. - Şirket, iç denetim çalışmalarının 2025 yılını da kapsayacak şekilde genişletildiğini ve ödemenin TMSF ile SPK ile yapılan görüşmeler sonucunda gönüllülük esasına göre gerçekleştirildiğini açıkladı. Türkiye Sigorta tarafından 13 Kasım 2026 tarihinde Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yapılan açıklamada, şirket bünyesinde yürütülen kapsamlı iç denetim ve inceleme çalışmalarına ilişkin bilgi verildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Açıklamada, 7 Ekim 2026 tarihli duyuruda belirtildiği üzere şirketin 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla tasfiyeye konu fonlarda bakiyesinin bulunmadığı hatırlatıldı. Bununla birlikte, 2025 yılını da kapsayacak şekilde genişletilen iç denetim çalışmaları sonucunda şirketin söz konusu fonların bir kısmına ilgili dönemde yürürlükte olan mevzuata ve yatırım politikasına uygun şekilde yatırım yaptığı ve bu yatırımlardan kazanç elde ettiği tespit edildi. 1,6 milyar TL'lik kazanç TMSF'ye aktarıldı Türkiye Sigorta, elde edilen kazançların mevzuata uygun olmasına rağmen şirketin etik ilkeleri ve hakkaniyet anlayışı doğrultusunda, TMSF ve SPK ile yapılan görüşmeler sonucunda gönüllü iade kararı aldığını bildirdi. İade tutarı hesaplanırken yatırım süresine isabet eden Yİ-ÜFE ve TÜFE oranlarının ortalaması üzerinden enflasyon etkisi düşüldü. Bu hesaplama sonucunda iade edilecek kazanç 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin 908 TL olarak belirlendi. Şirket, söz konusu tutarın 13 Kasım 2026 tarihinde TMSF hesabına yatırıldığını açıkladı. Başka ödeme yükümlülüğü beklenmiyor Şirket açıklamasında, söz konusu fonlara yapılan yatırımlarla ilgili başka bir iade veya ödeme yükümlülüğünün bulunmadığının öngörüldüğü belirtildi. Türkiye Sigorta ayrıca gerçekleştirilen ödemeye ilişkin yasal haklarının saklı olduğunu ve konuyla ilgili gelişmelerin kamuoyuyla paylaşılmaya devam edileceğini bildirdi. Türkiye Sigorta'nın açıklaması, tasfiyeye konu yatırım fonlarına yönelik incelemeler kapsamında gerçekleşen ödemelere ilişkin yeni bir gelişme oldu. Şirket, iade tutarının tamamının TMSF hesabına aktarıldığını ve hesaplamada enflasyon etkisinin düşüldüğünü özellikle vurguladı.

articles.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
articles.summary: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
articles.summaryTr: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
articles.articleText: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine - Published Russia's President Vladimir Putin says he wishes "eternal peace" for Ukraine. That is the same Russian president who ordered the full-scale invasion of Russia's neighbour nearly five years ago and who continues to reject the idea of a comprehensive ceasefire. And what, in Moscow's view, is a prerequisite for peace? The Kremlin spelt it out after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: "A new, long-term architecture of indivisible security and peace." Translated from Kremlin-speak, it means Moscow wants to change the security set-up of Europe in a way that benefits Russia. What Russia is pushing for is, potentially, the biggest change to European security arrangements since the end of the Cold War. The Kremlin has put back on the table its controversial proposal from December 2021 – the "draft treaties" with the US and Nato which would not only have put the brakes on the alliance's eastward enlargement by giving Moscow cast-iron guarantees that, for instance, Ukraine and Georgia would never be allowed to join, but also rolled back Nato military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. Western leaders dismissed such demands as an unacceptable Russian ultimatum. Two months later Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The "draft treaties" were put away. Now they are out of the geopolitical filing cabinet, and being quoted again by the Kremlin. What is more, Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy aide, has suggested that Moscow is about to "add certain new considerations" to its list of demands in light of Western efforts "to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia". That does not mean, of course, that Western governments will accept them. But the fact that the question of European security is featuring now in discussions on Ukraine is viewed here as a victory for Moscow. "In December 2021 Russia actively proposed that Nato rethink the security system in Europe," wrote newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda earlier this week. "Our proposals were almost laughed at. "Having secured one victory by forcing the West to think about security, our diplomats need a second by making the West heed Russia's concerns about Nato enlargement." The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, has called Russia's demands for a new European security architecture a "trap" designed to "shift attention away from a ceasefire". "The sequencing of Ukraine-Russia talks is important," Kallas wrote on social media. "The priority should be securing a ceasefire, followed by a peace agreement. Only then can there be discussions on Europe's wider security architecture." Europe's problem is that, right now, it is not at the table. Moscow has had no desire to give it a chair. It has slammed European leaders for their military support for Kyiv and tough stance on Russia. This week's peace talks in Abu Dhabi involved Ukraine, Russia and the US. After his discussions in Moscow, Witkoff indicated that Putin had agreed to the idea of European representatives joining the next round of Ukraine peace talks. But on Friday the Kremlin indicated a final decision on European participation had not been taken. "Once we understand their true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to take a decision about dialogue on Ukraine in a wider format," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. - Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks - Published17 hours ago - Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine - Published1 day ago - Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up - Published3 days ago And what of Putin? At the talks with Witkoff and Kushner he was sounding uncompromising and confident. You can see why. The Americans are knocking at his door and seeking a deal and the Europeans are contemplating contacts with him. Last month the leaders of Norway and Finland reached out and called him. And next week in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation summit, Putin may have a separate meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Russian media are already comparing them to the "Big Three" - Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill - who met in 1945 to reorganise post-World War Two Europe. And yet, after nearly five years of war, Russia has suffered huge losses on the battlefield. The Russian economy is under increasing pressure. Ukrainian drone strikes continue to target Russian oil refineries, sparking fears of new fuel shortages. But, so far, none of this has convinced the Kremlin leader to end the fighting.

But on Friday the Kremlin indicated a final decision on European participation had not been taken. "Once we understand their true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to take a decision about dialogue on Ukraine in a wider format," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. - Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks - Published17 hours ago - Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine - Published1 day ago - Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up - Published3 days ago And what of Putin? At the talks with Witkoff and Kushner he was sounding uncompromising and confident. You can see why. The Americans are knocking at his door and seeking a deal and the Europeans are contemplating contacts with him. Last month the leaders of Norway and Finland reached out and called him. And next week in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation summit, Putin may have a separate meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Russian media are already comparing them to the "Big Three" - Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill - who met in 1945 to reorganise post-World War Two Europe. And yet, after nearly five years of war, Russia has suffered huge losses on the battlefield. The Russian economy is under increasing pressure. Ukrainian drone strikes continue to target Russian oil refineries, sparking fears of new fuel shortages. But, so far, none of this has convinced the Kremlin leader to end the fighting.

articles.title: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9325-26 CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets November 13, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced that it has filed a lawsuit against Arkansas to block the state’s attempts to halt event-contract trading and impose up to hundreds of millions of dollars in civil penalties on CFTC-registered exchanges. Arkansas is bringing a civil enforcement against Kalshi in state court, a CFTC-designated contract market. Arkansas’s efforts to obstruct the functions of CFTC-registered exchanges operating lawfully under the Commodity Exchange Act are preempted by federal law. “As prediction markets continue to prove their value in being useful for risk management and providing the public with valuable information about the future, Arkansas seeks to shut down event contracts ranging from sports and politics to other important world events,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The CFTC will continue to defend its sole jurisdiction over these federally regulated markets as granted by Congress under the Commodity Exchange Act, and the Commission will not let state interference thwart its regulatory efforts and destroy federally regulated markets.” Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued to vindicate federal sovereign interests. The CFTC has also submitted amicus briefs in four federal Courts of Appeal and one state Supreme Court. -CFTC-

news.titleTr: Borsada şirketlerden peş peşe hamleler! Milyonluk anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar gündemde
news.summaryTr: Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören 8 şirket, yayımladıkları KAP açıklamalarıyla yeni iş ilişkileri, stratejik anlaşmalar ve yatırımlara imza attıklarını duyurdu.
news.articleText: Borsada şirketlerden peş peşe hamleler! Milyonluk anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar gündemde Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören 8 şirket, yayımladıkları KAP açıklamalarıyla yeni iş ilişkileri, stratejik anlaşmalar ve yatırımlara imza attıklarını duyurdu. LINK, 11,5 milyon TL'lik yüz tanıma kamerası projesini tamamladı Link Bilgisayar, Emniyet Genel Müdürlüğü ile imzaladığı 11 milyon 554 bin TL bedelli KGYS yüz tanıma kamerası projesini tamamladı. Şirket, teslimat ve faturalandırma işlemlerinin gerçekleştirildiğini KAP'a bildirdi. EUPWR, TEİAŞ ihalesinde 205,9 milyon TL'lik teklifle birinci oldu Europower Enerji, TEİAŞ'ın 152 adet metal clad hücre ve yedek malzeme alımı ihalesinde en avantajlı teklifi vererek ilk sırada yer aldı. İhalenin baz bedeli 205 milyon 917 bin TL olarak açıklandı. QNBFK'den 75 milyon euroluk kredi anlaşması QNB Finansal Kiralama, uluslararası kalkınma finansmanı kuruluşu Proparco ile 75 milyon euro tutarında kredi anlaşması imzaladı. news.title: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
news.summary: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge
news.summaryTr: Maryland Senator Van Hollen says "new leadership" is needed for Democrats following the party's recent midterm successes.
news.articleText: Democratic Senate leader Schumer set to face leadership challenge - Published Senator Chuck Schumer is facing a challenge to his position as US Senate majority leader from his fellow Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen, as the party prepares to take control of Congress after sweeping the midterm elections. Van Hollen, 67, said in a post on X on Thursday that Americans voted for change earlier this month and "to deliver, we need new leadership". Schumer, 75, has led Democrats in the chamber since 2017, serving as both majority and minority leader. He was first elected to the Senate in 1999. Following the midterms earlier this month, his position has come under pressure by some left-wing Democrats who see him as too moderate and part of the party establishment. Responding to the challenge, Schumer, who represents New York, said he welcomed "any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead". He added that he was "proud of what we've accomplished together" in the midterms, and he had "the votes to continue as Democratic leader". The vote on Senate leader will be held behind closed doors in early December and the winner will assume the role on 4 January, when Democrats take control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives after their midterms successes. The move by Van Hollen, who represents Maryland, marks the most significant step by a high-profile Democrat to challenge the party's existing leadership following last week's midterms victory. Announcing his plans to run in a post on X, he wrote that Americans had called on the party to "unrig an economy rigged against working people". "We should not be preserving our institutions if they are not delivering for the American people," he said at a summit in Colorado hosted by majority Democrats. "And we should be making delivering for the American people the single mission of our government, even when that means shaking things up." He added: "This country does not belong to the people who can afford to buy influence. It belongs to all of us. And it's time we govern like that." In recent years, Van Hollen has taken positions popular with those on the left of his party. In 2024, he supported restricting weapons shipments to Israel and criticised the Biden administration over its role in the war in Gaza. In an interview with MS NOW, Van Hollen - who has served in the Senate for nearly a decade - acknowledged that he was an "underdog" but added that he believed the race was "very much in flux". Independent Senator Bernie Sanders and Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed have both publicly come out in support of Van Hollen - while others have also called for new leadership. In a post on X, Sanders said he believed Van Hollen "will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families". El-Sayed said the challenger would bring "bold leadership" and lead with both "courage and experience". Others Democrats have publicly backed Schumer. Senator Jacky Rosen of Nevada said: "He has the experience and the fight to continue leading our diverse caucus at this crucial moment". Senator Kirsten Gillibrand said: "You will see, despite all the grumblings, enormous gratitude for the hard work he has done to get us to this position." - Published18 hours ago - Published1 day ago - Published2 days ago

news.titleTr: COP31’de sanat ve iklim krizi buluştu: Altı sanatçıdan ortak çağrı
news.summaryTr: Antalya’da düzenlenen COP31 kapsamında sanat ve iklim krizi COPArt’ta buluştu. Altı sanatçının eserlerinden oluşan seçki, geri dönüştürülmüş metallerden doğanın kırılganlığına uzanan çalışmalarla insanın çevreyle ilişkisini ve gezegenin geleceğini sorguluyor.
news.articleText: COP31’de sanat ve iklim krizi buluştu: Altı sanatçıdan ortak çağrı - Antalya’da düzenlenen COP31 kapsamında sanat ve iklim krizi COPArt’ta buluştu. Altı sanatçının eserlerinden oluşan seçki, geri dönüştürülmüş metallerden doğanın kırılganlığına uzanan çalışmalarla insanın çevreyle ilişkisini ve gezegenin geleceğini sorguluyor. RS Sanat Alanı, Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği 31. Taraflar Konferansı (COP31) kapsamında Antalya’da düzenlenen COPArt’ta sanatseverlerle buluşuyor. 20 Kasım’a kadar konferansın Green Zone ve Blue Zone alanlarında ziyaret edilebilen seçki; iklim acil durumunu, doğanın kırılganlığını ve insanın çevresi üzerindeki etkisini sanatın düşündüren, sorgulatan ve harekete geçiren diliyle gündeme taşıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle RS Sanat Alanı, COPArt’taki seçkisiyle iklim acil durumuna ilişkin tartışmalara sanatın özgün bakışını da katıyor. Sanatçılara verdiği destekle farklı ifade biçimlerine alan açarken ziyaretçileri ortak bir soru etrafında buluşturuyor: Doğayla kurduğumuz ilişkiyi değiştirmek için neyi görmemiz, neyi hatırlamamız ve neyi dönüştürmemiz gerekiyor? Asaf Erdemli, Berkan Baycan, Ceylan Sakin Dökmen, Gönül Nuhoğlu, İsmet Doğan ve Murat Uçar’ın eserlerini, COP31 katılımcılarıyla buluşturan RS Sanat Alanı, farklı sanat pratiklerinin çevresel ve toplumsal meseleler etrafında diyalog kurmasına destek veriyor. Doğa, hafıza, dönüşüm ve aidiyet kavramları etrafında şekillenen çalışmalar, ziyaretçilerin insanın dünyadaki yerine ve diğer canlılarla ilişkisine yeniden bakmasını sağlıyor. Asaf Erdemli, “Bu İşte Bir Terslik Var” adlı enstalasyonunda Türkiye’nin doğal ve kültürel mirasının simgelerinden ters laleyi, geri dönüştürülmüş metaller aracılığıyla yeniden yorumluyor. COP31 kapsamında özel olarak üretilen 31 adet ters lale heykelinden oluşan enstalasyon, üretim ve tüketim alışkanlıklarımızı sorgularken, atıl malzemelerin yeniden değer kazanmasına dikkat çekiyor. Sanatçı, geri dönüşümü yalnızca bir üretim yöntemi olarak değil, doğaya ve geleceğe karşı kolektif bir sorumluluk olarak ele alıyor. Berkan Baycan’ın “Observer” adlı video çalışmasında bakışın yönü değişiyor: İnsan doğayı izlerken doğa da insanın yaptıklarına tanıklık ediyor. İnsan merkezli düşünceyi sorgulayan eser, ziyaretçiyi doğadaki dönüşümün sorumluluğunu paylaşan bir aktör olarak kendi konumunu değerlendirmeye çağırıyor. Ceylan Sakin Dökmen’in “Güneş Ağacı”, “Rüzgara Kapıldım” ve “Ağıt Ağaç” adlı metal heykelleri, doğanın kırılganlığı ile yenilenme gücünü aynı yüzeyde buluşturuyor. Eserlerdeki çatlaklar ve boşluklar, kırılmanın izlerini taşırken yeniden oluşun ihtimalini de barındırıyor. Sanatçı, metalin sertliği üzerinden doğanın hassas dengelerine dikkat çekiyor. Gönül Nuhoğlu’nun “Dreaming Rhino” adlı çalışmasındaki uyuyan gergedan, iklim krizi karşısındaki kolektif kayıtsızlığın simgesine dönüşüyor. Eser, büyüyen tehditlerin gündelik yaşam içinde nasıl sıradanlaştığını sorgularken izleyiciyi kendi duyarsızlıklarıyla yüzleşmeye davet ediyor. İnsan doğaya baktığında yalnızca çevresini değil, kendi kökenlerini de görüyor. İsmet Doğan, “Kök-en” ve “Autos” serisinde insanın doğayla, geçmişiyle ve kendi varoluşuyla kurduğu bağı sorguluyor. Kökler, doğaya ait bir yaşam kaynağı olmanın yanı sıra hafızanın, kimliğin ve aidiyetin simgesi olarak beliriyor. İzleyiciyi kendi yansımasıyla eserin bir parçasına dönüştüren sanatçı, insanın doğayla bir bütün olduğunu hatırlatıyor. İklim krizinin doğayla kurduğumuz ilişkiyi yeniden düşünmeye zorladığı günümüzde, “Kök-en” temel bir soruyu gündeme getiriyor: İnsan, kendi köklerinden ne kadar uzaklaşabilir? Murat Uçar’ın eserleri, Türkiye tarihinde ilklere imza atmış 36 ismin yaşamına büyüteç aracılığıyla yakından bakmaya davet ediyor. Kolektif hafızayı şekillendiren öncü figürleri yeniden görünür kılan eserler, değişimin ardındaki insan hikâyelerini seçkinin odağına taşıyor.

Gönül Nuhoğlu’nun “Dreaming Rhino” adlı çalışmasındaki uyuyan gergedan, iklim krizi karşısındaki kolektif kayıtsızlığın simgesine dönüşüyor. Eser, büyüyen tehditlerin gündelik yaşam içinde nasıl sıradanlaştığını sorgularken izleyiciyi kendi duyarsızlıklarıyla yüzleşmeye davet ediyor. İnsan doğaya baktığında yalnızca çevresini değil, kendi kökenlerini de görüyor. İsmet Doğan, “Kök-en” ve “Autos” serisinde insanın doğayla, geçmişiyle ve kendi varoluşuyla kurduğu bağı sorguluyor. Kökler, doğaya ait bir yaşam kaynağı olmanın yanı sıra hafızanın, kimliğin ve aidiyetin simgesi olarak beliriyor. İzleyiciyi kendi yansımasıyla eserin bir parçasına dönüştüren sanatçı, insanın doğayla bir bütün olduğunu hatırlatıyor. İklim krizinin doğayla kurduğumuz ilişkiyi yeniden düşünmeye zorladığı günümüzde, “Kök-en” temel bir soruyu gündeme getiriyor: İnsan, kendi köklerinden ne kadar uzaklaşabilir? Murat Uçar’ın eserleri, Türkiye tarihinde ilklere imza atmış 36 ismin yaşamına büyüteç aracılığıyla yakından bakmaya davet ediyor. Kolektif hafızayı şekillendiren öncü figürleri yeniden görünür kılan eserler, değişimin ardındaki insan hikâyelerini seçkinin odağına taşıyor.

news.titleTr: BMW'den 721 bin araç için yangın alarmı! Park uyarısı geldi
news.summaryTr: ABD Ulusal Kara Yolu Trafik Güvenliği İdaresi (NHTSA), yangın riski nedeniyle BMW'nin yaklaşık 721 bin aracını geri çağırdığını duyurdu. Araç sahiplerine, onarım işlemi tamamlanana kadar otomobillerini açık alana park etmeleri uyarısı yapıldı.
news.articleText: BMW'den 721 bin araç için yangın alarmı! Park uyarısı geldi - ABD Ulusal Kara Yolu Trafik Güvenliği İdaresi (NHTSA), yangın riski nedeniyle BMW'nin yaklaşık 721 bin aracını geri çağırdığını duyurdu. - Araç sahiplerine, onarım işlemi tamamlanana kadar otomobillerini açık alana park etmeleri uyarısı yapıldı. ABD Ulusal Kara Yolu Trafik Güvenliği İdaresi (NHTSA), Alman otomobil üreticisi BMW'nin 720 bin 796 aracını yangın riski nedeniyle geri çağırdığını açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle NHTSA tarafından yapılan açıklamada, söz konusu araçların park halindeyken ve motoru kapalıyken de yangın riski taşıdığı belirtildi. Araç sahiplerine, gerekli onarım tamamlanana kadar otomobillerini binalardan ve diğer araçlardan uzakta, açık alanlara park etmeleri tavsiye edildi. 2024'te de geri çağrılmışlardı Açıklamada, geri çağırma kapsamındaki araçların 2024 yılında su pompası kaynaklı bir sorun nedeniyle de servise çağrıldığı hatırlatıldı. Mevcut sorunun giderilmesi için araçların yeniden onarılması gerektiği bildirildi. Soruna yönelik çözümün henüz geliştirme aşamasında olduğu belirtilirken, onarım hizmetinin hazır olduğunda BMW yetkili servislerinde ücretsiz olarak sunulacağı kaydedildi. Geri çağırma hangi BMW modellerini kapsıyor? Geri çağırma kararı, 2012-2016 model yılları arasındaki bazı BMW 3 Series ve 5 Series araçlarının yanı sıra X1, X3, X4 ve X5 modellerini de kapsıyor. NHTSA'nın açıkladığı listede ayrıca Z4, 2 Series ve 4 Series modellerinin belirli üretim yıllarındaki coupe, convertible, Gran Coupe ve Sportswagon versiyonları da yer alıyor. Geri çağırma kapsamındaki araç sahiplerinin, araçlarının bu listede bulunup bulunmadığını şasi numarası (VIN) üzerinden kontrol etmesi ve onarım süreciyle ilgili BMW'den gelecek bilgilendirmeleri takip etmesi gerekiyor.

news.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
news.summary: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
news.summaryTr: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.
news.articleText: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost? - Published A major Microsoft outage has impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world. Services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot, are being restored almost 24 hours since issues first surfaced. Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue. It has apologised for the disruption. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. What happened? Some Microsoft 365 services have been affected by "connectivity problems" with problems reported in at least 74 countries. From late on Thursday, customers reported varying levels of access - many were unable to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. But some users were able to use Teams, messaging and online meeting functions without issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added that it was focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" but warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues". In a later statement, the company said it was continuing to see improvements "with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels". The company attributed the ongoing outage to an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions," it said on Friday. Will emails affected by the outage ever arrive? Although services are beginning to resume, Microsoft has warned of continued "intermittent access issues", meaning some users will still struggle to load their inboxes and could experience "delayed email delivery". In other words, it is not quite safe to assume every email you send is going to arrive in its intended recipient's inbox right away. Earlier, Microsoft said it would be extending the "timeout window" to 48 hours "to help protect delayed messages as delivery catches up". The email timeout window refers to the amount of time Outlook will wait to receive an email. When they do show up, the timestamp will be when they were delivered rather than when they were sent. Why has it taken so long to fix? Although email service Outlook appears to be resuming, the outage has so far lasted for more than 20 hours - in outage terms that is considered a long time. Prof James Ferryman from the University of Reading's department of computer science said the details the company has disclosed provide some clues. "What Microsoft has told us is that the part of its servers that sets up secure connections is getting swamped, and once that happens the server just stops answering," he said. "The trouble is that this kind of failure snowballs. "One server falls over, its work gets passed to the next one, and meanwhile huge numbers of phones and laptops keep trying to get back in. "You can't just turn it all back on at once. You have to bring it back bit by bit." The challenge is therefore not just fixing the fault, but managing the huge surge of devices trying to reconnect once services start coming back online. Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time". He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal. Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. "Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. "Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said. In a statement, Microsoft said it was "deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. "We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services." How many people have been affected? More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website. The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed. Microsoft 365 is used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services. Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic both earlier reported problems as a result of the outage. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which had caused some tools to not work as expected. From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread. Courts from Los Angeles to Texas earlier warned that communications might be delayed. In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected. The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted. Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage. Some GP surgeries had urged patients not to submit messages via their website while police forces were also earlier asking the public to call if they want to make a report. Additional reporting by Henry Moore Get in touch Have you or your business been affected by the outage?

news.title: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
news.summary: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
news.summaryTr: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.
news.articleText: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own - Published Pope Leo XIV has celebrated mass near the Peruvian city where he made his name as a compassionate bishop who worked closely with poor and migrant communities. The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff. "Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers. "Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago. Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the mass began. "We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique. Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend. Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting. Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional. The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached. They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C. For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight. "The Pope has come home and Chiclayo is celebrating," said Lisbeth Díaz, a teacher who worked with Pope Leo when he served as the city's bishop between 2015 and 2023. Peru is the longest stop on the first tour of Latin America by the pontiff, who was elected in May 2025. The trip has also taken in Argentina and Uruguay, but his time in this country carries particular significance. The Pope not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities. Around Chiclayo, it is hard to meet anyone who doesn't claim to be a friend of the Pope or have a special anecdote about him. Some recall how he would enjoy sampling Peruvian delicacies at El Trébol, a restaurant next to the city's cathedral. Others remember his love of tennis. But for many it's the more serious moments of his time here, such as helping launch soup kitchens during the Covid-19 pandemic, or wading through deep waters on horseback when floods hit the area. Several of these images are on display in a small museum dedicated to him at the entrance to the bishop's residence. But for the city, and for a country that calls him the "Peruvian Pope", his return home means much more than a collection of photographs and anecdotes. "It is the return of the man who brought Peruvians closer to the Church," said Samuel David Miranda Atoche, a local parish priest from Chiclayo who was ordained by the Pope back when he was still the bishop and known under his birth name of Robert Prevost. And it is not just local people he connected with, according to Díaz, who came to Chiclayo from Venezuela. "It was difficult for him to see so many migrants living on the streets," she added, recalling the time when large numbers of Venezuelans came through Chiclayo escaping the political and economic crisis in their home country. "So, he got in touch with the migration authorities and coordinated with other organisations to speed up the paperwork needed for many of us to obtain legal residency and work permits." - Who is Robert Prevost, the new Pope Leo XIV? - Published9 May 2025 Robert Prevost's time here as bishop also involved difficult decisions, such as having to deal with the controversy and scandal surrounding the dissolution of Sodalitium of Christian Life, a Peruvian Catholic organisation that had faced decades of sexual abuse allegations. Santiago Roncagliolo, a Peruvian writer and journalist who has studied the Pope's life, believes his handling of that crisis earned him the favour of his predecessor, Pope Francis, and helped set him on the path to the papacy. Father David also stressed the role the now-pontiff played in bringing people together. "If there is one thing Bishop Prevost worked for here," he added, referring to the Pope by his previous title, "it was unity". That unity has been on display in the run up to the mass, with the square in front of Chiclayo Cathedral filled with joyous celebrations for days. Normally, 800,000 people live in the city and its surrounding area, but estimates say the Pope's visit has caused that to double. Local businesses have been capitalising on the Pope's popularity to boost sales and hotels have sharply increased their nightly room rates. But that didn't seem to put off the faithful who gathered for the mass. Shouts of: "The Pope is from Chiclayo!" echoed across the field during the event. Their affection was clearly reflected by the pontiff. "As I look at your faces, a prayer of thanksgiving to the Lord arises in my heart," he said from the stage, "for the blessing you have been and continue to be in my life." The ceremony was held on Friday at a park in Pimentel, about 10km (six miles) from Chiclayo in northern Peru as part of his tour of Latin America. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff. "Thank you for your affection, support and prayers," the Pope told followers. "Especially for my health during this time of trial which, with God's help, I am overcoming," he added, referencing the surgery he had for lung cancer which took place just weeks ago. Some of the crowd arrived 12 hours in advance to wait in vigil before the mass began. "We spent the night praying, alongside family, excited to welcome the Pope from Chiclayo," said Isa Orderique. Many came from across Peru and even neighbouring countries to attend. Merli Cruz Guerrero, from an area near the Ecuadorean border, travelled several hours by bus to attend. She also spent the entire night waiting. Of all the events the Pope has attended so far during his visit to Peru, this felt particularly emotional. The crowd fell into a hushed silence as the pontiff's motorcade approached. They waited eagerly for his arrival despite spending long hours out in the open with the temperature pushing past 30C. For many living here, the fact that the Pope worked extensively in this region before becoming the head of the Catholic Church has put them in the spotlight. news.summaryTr: 12-13 Kasım tarihlerinde 3 şirket, farklı kurumsal işlemler kapsamında Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'na (SPK) başvurduğunu KAP üzerinden duyurdu. Başvurular arasında halka arz, kolaylaştırılmış birleşme ve kayıtlı sermaye tavanı artırımı öne çıktı.
news.articleText: 3 şirketten SPK'ya başvuru! Halka arz, birleşme ve sermaye tavanı hamleleri - 12-13 Kasım tarihlerinde 3 şirket, farklı kurumsal işlemler kapsamında Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'na (SPK) başvurduğunu KAP üzerinden duyurdu. - Başvurular arasında halka arz, kolaylaştırılmış birleşme ve kayıtlı sermaye tavanı artırımı öne çıktı. SPK'ya üç şirketten halka arz, birleşme ve sermaye tavanı başvurusu geldi. Başvurular arasında yeni bir halka arz hazırlığı da yer aldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 12-13 Kasım 2026 tarihlerinde SPK'ya başvuru yapan şirketler ve başvuru konuları şöyle: Investco Holding (INVES) Investco Holding'in yüzde 100 bağlı ortaklığı REM Girişim Sermayesi Yatırım Ortaklığı'nın halka arz başvurusu, 12 Kasım 2026 tarihinde SPK'ya yapıldı. Ata Turizm (ATATR) Ata Turizm, yüzde 100 bağlı ortaklıkları Gökyüzü Balonculuk Taşımacılık Hizmetleri ve Kapadokya Balonculuk Ticaret Turizm şirketlerini devralmak üzere SPK'ya başvurdu. Başvuru, iki şirketin tüm aktif ve pasifleriyle birlikte tasfiyesiz şekilde Ata Turizm bünyesinde birleştirilmesini kapsıyor. Birleşmenin kolaylaştırılmış usulde gerçekleştirilmesi planlanıyor. Loras Holding (LRSHO) Loras Holding, kayıtlı sermaye tavanını 1,2 milyar TL'den 15 milyar TL'ye yükseltmek için SPK ve Ticaret Bakanlığına başvurma kararı aldı. Yeni kayıtlı sermaye tavanının 2027-2031 yılları arasında 5 yıl süreyle geçerli olması planlanıyor. Bu kapsamda şirket esas sözleşmesinin sermayeye ilişkin 7. maddesinin değiştirilmesi de kararlaştırıldı. Kayıtlı sermaye tavanı, şirketlerin esas sözleşmelerinde belirlenen ve yönetim kurulu kararıyla çıkarılmış sermayenin artırılabileceği üst sınırı ifade ediyor. Tavanın yükseltilmesi doğrudan sermaye artırımı yapıldığı anlamına gelmiyor.

Borsa İstanbul'da şirketlerin finansal raporlarını mevzuatta belirlenen sürelerde KAP'a açıklaması gerekiyor. news.titleTr: Türkiye Sigorta'dan fon soruşturması kapsamında 1,6 milyar TL'lik ödeme
news.summaryTr: Türkiye Sigorta (TURSG), tasfiyeye konu bazı yatırım fonlarından elde ettiği kazancın 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin 908 TL'lik bölümünü TMSF'ye iade etti.
news.articleText: Türkiye Sigorta'dan fon soruşturması kapsamında 1,6 milyar TL'lik ödeme - Türkiye Sigorta (TURSG), tasfiyeye konu bazı yatırım fonlarından elde ettiği kazancın 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin 908 TL'lik bölümünü TMSF'ye iade etti. - Şirket, iç denetim çalışmalarının 2025 yılını da kapsayacak şekilde genişletildiğini ve ödemenin TMSF ile SPK ile yapılan görüşmeler sonucunda gönüllülük esasına göre gerçekleştirildiğini açıkladı. Türkiye Sigorta tarafından 13 Kasım 2026 tarihinde Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yapılan açıklamada, şirket bünyesinde yürütülen kapsamlı iç denetim ve inceleme çalışmalarına ilişkin bilgi verildi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Açıklamada, 7 Ekim 2026 tarihli duyuruda belirtildiği üzere şirketin 30 Eylül 2026 itibarıyla tasfiyeye konu fonlarda bakiyesinin bulunmadığı hatırlatıldı. Bununla birlikte, 2025 yılını da kapsayacak şekilde genişletilen iç denetim çalışmaları sonucunda şirketin söz konusu fonların bir kısmına ilgili dönemde yürürlükte olan mevzuata ve yatırım politikasına uygun şekilde yatırım yaptığı ve bu yatırımlardan kazanç elde ettiği tespit edildi. 1,6 milyar TL'lik kazanç TMSF'ye aktarıldı Türkiye Sigorta, elde edilen kazançların mevzuata uygun olmasına rağmen şirketin etik ilkeleri ve hakkaniyet anlayışı doğrultusunda, TMSF ve SPK ile yapılan görüşmeler sonucunda gönüllü iade kararı aldığını bildirdi. İade tutarı hesaplanırken yatırım süresine isabet eden Yİ-ÜFE ve TÜFE oranlarının ortalaması üzerinden enflasyon etkisi düşüldü. news.title: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
news.summary: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine
news.summaryTr: The fact the question of European security now features in discussions is viewed in Moscow as a victory, BBC Russia Editor Steve Rosenberg says.
news.articleText: Rosenberg: Uncompromising Putin ups demands for peace with Ukraine - Published Russia's President Vladimir Putin says he wishes "eternal peace" for Ukraine. That is the same Russian president who ordered the full-scale invasion of Russia's neighbour nearly five years ago and who continues to reject the idea of a comprehensive ceasefire. And what, in Moscow's view, is a prerequisite for peace? The Kremlin spelt it out after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner: "A new, long-term architecture of indivisible security and peace." Translated from Kremlin-speak, it means Moscow wants to change the security set-up of Europe in a way that benefits Russia. What Russia is pushing for is, potentially, the biggest change to European security arrangements since the end of the Cold War. The Kremlin has put back on the table its controversial proposal from December 2021 – the "draft treaties" with the US and Nato which would not only have put the brakes on the alliance's eastward enlargement by giving Moscow cast-iron guarantees that, for instance, Ukraine and Georgia would never be allowed to join, but also rolled back Nato military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe which became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union. Western leaders dismissed such demands as an unacceptable Russian ultimatum. Two months later Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The "draft treaties" were put away. Now they are out of the geopolitical filing cabinet, and being quoted again by the Kremlin. What is more, Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign policy aide, has suggested that Moscow is about to "add certain new considerations" to its list of demands in light of Western efforts "to inflict a strategic defeat on Russia". That does not mean, of course, that Western governments will accept them. But the fact that the question of European security is featuring now in discussions on Ukraine is viewed here as a victory for Moscow. "In December 2021 Russia actively proposed that Nato rethink the security system in Europe," wrote newspaper Komsomolskaya Pravda earlier this week. "Our proposals were almost laughed at. "Having secured one victory by forcing the West to think about security, our diplomats need a second by making the West heed Russia's concerns about Nato enlargement." The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, has called Russia's demands for a new European security architecture a "trap" designed to "shift attention away from a ceasefire". "The sequencing of Ukraine-Russia talks is important," Kallas wrote on social media. "The priority should be securing a ceasefire, followed by a peace agreement. Only then can there be discussions on Europe's wider security architecture." Europe's problem is that, right now, it is not at the table. Moscow has had no desire to give it a chair. It has slammed European leaders for their military support for Kyiv and tough stance on Russia. This week's peace talks in Abu Dhabi involved Ukraine, Russia and the US. After his discussions in Moscow, Witkoff indicated that Putin had agreed to the idea of European representatives joining the next round of Ukraine peace talks. But on Friday the Kremlin indicated a final decision on European participation had not been taken. "Once we understand their true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to take a decision about dialogue on Ukraine in a wider format," said Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov. - Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks - Published17 hours ago - Europe's security 'fundamentally reshaped' by war in Ukraine - Published1 day ago - Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up - Published3 days ago And what of Putin? At the talks with Witkoff and Kushner he was sounding uncompromising and confident. You can see why. The Americans are knocking at his door and seeking a deal and the Europeans are contemplating contacts with him. Last month the leaders of Norway and Finland reached out and called him. And next week in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation summit, Putin may have a separate meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Russian media are already comparing them to the "Big Three" - Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill - who met in 1945 to reorganise post-World War Two Europe. And yet, after nearly five years of war, Russia has suffered huge losses on the battlefield. The Russian economy is under increasing pressure. Ukrainian drone strikes continue to target Russian oil refineries, sparking fears of new fuel shortages. But, so far, none of this has convinced the Kremlin leader to end the fighting.

news.title: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9325-26 CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets November 13, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced that it has filed a lawsuit against Arkansas to block the state’s attempts to halt event-contract trading and impose up to hundreds of millions of dollars in civil penalties on CFTC-registered exchanges. Arkansas is bringing a civil enforcement against Kalshi in state court, a CFTC-designated contract market. Arkansas’s efforts to obstruct the functions of CFTC-registered exchanges operating lawfully under the Commodity Exchange Act are preempted by federal law. “As prediction markets continue to prove their value in being useful for risk management and providing the public with valuable information about the future, Arkansas seeks to shut down event contracts ranging from sports and politics to other important world events,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The CFTC will continue to defend its sole jurisdiction over these federally regulated markets as granted by Congress under the Commodity Exchange Act, and the Commission will not let state interference thwart its regulatory efforts and destroy federally regulated markets.” Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued to vindicate federal sovereign interests. The CFTC has also submitted amicus briefs in four federal Courts of Appeal and one state Supreme Court. -CFTC-
